remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided showing that the initial rollout excludes the affected small-business onboarding use case.
No new admissible evidence was provided showing reviewed and approved risk acceptance that specifically covers the exposed small-business onboarding segment.
The actor's narrowed position is operationally caveated, but the missing exclusion-or-approval condition remains an unresolved compliance predicate under the stated policy.

Evidence access is limited to the actor summary, so there is still no admissible record here showing the required model-card disclosure or approval artifact was actually completed before certification.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is more accurate and appropriately rejects the unsupported claim that rollout limits, rollback, dashboards, or monitoring alone satisfy policy. But it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat is not merely a disclosure nuance or bounded limitation; it is the unresolved policy condition itself. Under the stated policy, rollout controls mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance covers the exposure. On the available record, the small-business onboarding segment remains exposed and the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and not shown approved. That leaves certification not adequately supported as policy-compliant on admissible evidence, even if a monitored, reversible launch posture is operationally describable.
